author: Bobby Grayson
description: Loom.Tools.Shell (collect_output/3), Ensemble.AI.TextGenerator (collect_output/3), Loom.Teams.Debate (do_collect/6) and Loom.Session.Architect (a receive inside a case arm of check_editor_permission/3) all look one generalisation away: allow a loop of arity n and make its state an n-tuple, which the model already has. That would be WRONG for every one of them. Each is a synchronous collect: the caller uses the value the receive block returns (extract_result(buffer), {:error, :timeout}, the accumulated responses, :allowed | :denied). The translator's rule for a loop body that does not tail-call the loop is 'the loop returns, so the process exits :normal' -- which would claim the process dies where in fact the caller goes on. So the arity-1 restriction stays, and the new tail-position check makes explicit what it was standing in for: a receive is a process only when it is the whole life of one.
title: Multi-argument receive helpers are NOT raw-process loops, and I deliberately did not make them one
